records.name: Flexible Input
records.definition: The degree to which strictly validating every payload rejects the loosely-shaped input a caller might legitimately send.

records.name: Untyped Payloads
records.definition: Accepting data at a boundary with no schema, so malformed or unexpected shapes flow in unchecked.

records.name: Dynamic Untyped Boundaries

distinctFrom.reason: Untyped boundaries pass untyped values between modules, while stringly typed programming encodes states and types as strings anywhere in the code.

records.definition: Passing untyped values across module or service boundaries, so type errors surface only at runtime.

records.name: Explicit Types
records.definition: The requirement that values crossing a boundary carry explicit, declared types rather than open-ended ones.

records.name: Rapid Scripting
records.definition: The degree to which requiring explicit types slows the quick, exploratory coding that dynamic typing allows.

records.name: Bounded Context Autonomy
records.definition: The degree to which enforcing one canonical model limits each bounded context's freedom to model its own domain.

records.name: Multiple Competing Models
records.definition: Several inconsistent models of the same concept coexisting, so translations between them drift and conflict.

records.name: Normalized Translation
records.definition: The ability to translate between systems through one shared canonical form rather than many pairwise mappings.

records.name: Bounded Context Purity

distinctFrom.reason: Bounded context purity is each context's concepts staying clean, while local model autonomy is each context being free to evolve its own model.

records.definition: The degree to which sharing one enterprise data model erodes the conceptual purity of each bounded context.

records.name: Cross-System Mapping
records.definition: The ability to map data between systems through a single shared canonical representation.

records.name: Local Model Autonomy
records.definition: The degree to which a bounded context is free to define and evolve its own data model independently of a shared canonical one.

records.name: Service-Specific Schemas
records.definition: The degree to which a shared canonical schema competes with each service's need for its own tailored schema.

records.name: Ambiguous Encoding
records.definition: Representing the same value in multiple encodings without normalizing, so equal values compare as different.

records.name: Canonical Format
records.definition: The requirement that a single normalized form be defined for values before they are compared or stored.

records.name: Deduplication
records.definition: The ability to recognize and collapse values that are equivalent once reduced to canonical form.

records.name: Lossless Preservation
records.definition: The degree to which reducing values to a canonical form can discard distinctions the original preserved.

records.name: Security Checks
records.definition: The ability to apply security checks reliably by first reducing input to one unambiguous form.

records.name: Canonical Definition
records.definition: The requirement that each fact have one authoritative definition that all consumers reference.

records.name: Duplicated Authority

distinctFrom.reason: Duplicated authority is two owners for one fact, while a claimed foreign tree is governing names another runtime owns.
Duplicated authority is two owners for one fact, while a depth-relief container is a container declared to shorten a path.
Duplicated authority is two owning copies of a fact, while a magic value is a fact written as an unexplained literal, however many times.
Duplicated authority is two owners for one fact, while ignore-list silencing removes a file from the taxonomy to hide a finding.

records.definition: Two or more places each claiming to own the same fact, so they drift and disagree over time.

records.name: Data Semantics
records.definition: The requirement that the meaning and dependencies of data be understood before it is decomposed into relations.

records.name: Denormalized Read Models
records.definition: A read-optimized model that deliberately duplicates data to serve queries fast, trading storage and write cost for read speed.

records.name: Non-Redundant Storage
records.definition: The ability to store each fact once, so it cannot drift out of sync with copies and no update anomaly can arise.

records.name: Query Performance
records.definition: The degree to which splitting data across normalized relations forces costly joins on read.

records.name: Reduced Redundancy
records.definition: The ability to eliminate duplicated facts by referencing a single stored copy.

records.name: Disambiguation
records.definition: The ability to give each concept one unambiguous name and meaning across a domain.

records.name: Polysemy Across Contexts
records.definition: The degree to which one term legitimately carries different meanings in different bounded contexts.

records.name: Cross-Context Terminology
records.definition: The degree to which agreeing on shared terms strains against the distinct vocabularies different contexts need.

records.name: Domain Collaboration
records.definition: The requirement that domain experts and developers collaborate to agree on shared terminology.

records.name: Technical/Domain Mismatch
records.definition: Naming code in technical terms disconnected from the domain, so experts and developers talk past each other.

records.name: Ambiguous API

distinctFrom.reason: An ambiguous API hides what an interface does by any means, while a boolean trap is the case of boolean parameters hiding intent at the call site.

records.definition: An interface whose names and parameters hide what it does, so callers must guess or read the implementation.

records.name: Clear Semantics
records.definition: The requirement that an interface's names convey what each operation does and expects.

records.name: Concise Naming
records.definition: The degree to which naming an interface fully for clarity works against keeping names short.

records.name: Correct Usage
records.definition: The ability of callers to use an interface correctly because its names reveal its intent.

records.name: Naming Consistency

distinctFrom.reason: Naming consistency is one name per concept across an interface, while a set-relative member name leaves out what its folder already says.
Naming consistency is the same concept always getting the same name, while clear semantics is each name saying what the operation does.

records.definition: The requirement that names for the same concept be used consistently across an interface.

records.name: Clever Abstractions
records.definition: The degree to which clever, non-obvious abstractions trade familiarity for surprise to the reader.

records.name: Convention
records.definition: The requirement that a design follow shared naming, placement and behavior conventions, so its parts can be found automatically and behave as expected.

records.name: Safe Use
records.definition: The ability to use an interface safely because it behaves the way its name and shape suggest.

records.name: Duplicated Denormalized Columns
records.definition: The same fact copied into many columns and rows, so updates must touch every copy or leave them inconsistent.

records.name: Functional Dependencies
records.definition: The requirement that the dependencies determining which attributes fix others be identified before decomposing a schema.

records.name: Read Performance
records.definition: The degree to which normalizing a schema into many relations forces joins that slow reads.

records.name: Introduce Discriminated Union
records.definition: A technique for modeling a value that takes one of several shapes as a union whose variants carry a tag the type checker reads.

records.name: Narrow Type
records.definition: A technique for replacing a broad type with one that admits only the values the domain allows.

records.name: Define Absence Semantics
records.definition: A technique for choosing one representation for a missing value and stating what it means at the boundary.

records.name: Binary Schema Encoding
records.definition: A technique for serializing messages in a compact binary format whose schema the reader and writer share.

records.name: Schema Registry
records.definition: A technique for storing every published schema and its versions in one registry that producers and consumers check against.
